div.div: Potential evidence completeness for High-relevance mapped datamodels: recommended CIM fields present in scope, not compliance scores.

div.p: What this shows: High-relevance (primary) controls per framework, stacked by recommended CIM field completeness for that control’s single primary datamodel.
Why it matters: Each control has one High-relevance primary datamodel. Recommended fields are the minimum set that datamodel expects to be useful. Shared fields still count fully when present.
Read it as: Good Coverage = ≥70% recommended fields; Partial Coverage = 40-69%; Low Coverage = 1-39% (often thin or shared-field hits); No Coverage = 0%. Potential evidence gaps only, not compliance.

search.query: | chart count over framework by evidence_band | fillnull value=0 "Good Coverage" "Partial Coverage" "Low Coverage" "No Coverage" | table framework "Good Coverage" "Partial Coverage" "Low Coverage" "No Coverage" | sort framework

div.p: What this shows: All High-relevance primary controls in scope, grouped by recommended-field completeness band.
Why it matters: Separates strong coverage from partial, low/trace, and missing evidence so thin shared-field hits do not look the same as useful coverage.
Read it as: Potential evidence mix only, not compliance status or control effectiveness.

search.query: | stats count as controls by evidence_band | eval band_order=case(evidence_band="Good Coverage",1,evidence_band="Partial Coverage",2,evidence_band="Low Coverage",3,evidence_band="No Coverage",4,true(),5) | sort band_order | fields - band_order

div.p: What this shows: Per-framework counts of High-relevance primary controls in each completeness band, plus Recommended Field Coverage and Matched Datamodels (primary DMs with coverage greater than 0%).
Why it matters: Connects the stacked gap view to control counts and completeness for drill-down into Governance IN.
Read it as: Potential evidence summary only, not framework compliance or audit assurance. Each control uses one primary High-relevance datamodel.

search.query: | stats dc(control_reference) as mapped_controls dc(eval(if(evidence_band="Good Coverage",control_reference,null()))) as good_controls dc(eval(if(evidence_band="Partial Coverage",control_reference,null()))) as partial_controls dc(eval(if(evidence_band="Low Coverage",control_reference,null()))) as low_controls dc(eval(if(evidence_band="No Coverage",control_reference,null()))) as none_controls avg(control_coverage_pct) as avg_coverage_pct dc(capability) as mapped_capabilities dc(eval(if(control_coverage_pct>0,primary_datamodel,null()))) as matched_datamodels by framework framework_version | eval avg_coverage_pct=round(avg_coverage_pct,1) | rename framework as Framework framework_version as Version mapped_controls as "Primary Controls" good_controls as "Good Coverage" partial_controls as "Partial Coverage" low_controls as "Low Coverage" none_controls as "No Coverage" avg_coverage_pct as "Recommended Field Coverage" mapped_capabilities as "Mapped Capabilities" matched_datamodels as "Matched Datamodels" | table Framework Version "Primary Controls" "Good Coverage" "Partial Coverage" "Low Coverage" "No Coverage" "Recommended Field Coverage" "Mapped Capabilities" "Matched Datamodels" | sort - "Good Coverage" Framework

div.p: What this shows: Per data source: strongest High-relevance datamodel field evidence, how observed CIM models split between primary / supporting / unmapped, unique matched CIM fields, and which frameworks those mappings touch.
Why it matters: Source-level view behind the framework charts: which telemetry is carrying the potential evidence.
Read it as: Numbers in brackets are matched CIM fields for that datamodel. Potential evidence only, not compliance. Drill into Governance IN for control-level detail.

"|%") | eval is_primary_dm=if(governance_relevance="High",1,0) | stats max(is_primary_dm) as is_primary_dm values(framework) as dm_frameworks by datamodel | eval governance_mapped=1 ] | eval governance_mapped=coalesce(governance_mapped,0) | eval is_primary_dm=coalesce(is_primary_dm,0) | appendpipe [ | where is_primary_dm=1 | sort group_value - dm_field_hits | streamstats count as dm_rank by group_value | where dm_rank<=3 | eval top_item=datamodel . " (" . dm_field_hits . " fields)" | stats list(top_item) as strongest_evidence_mv by group_value | eval strongest_evidence=mvjoin(strongest_evidence_mv, "; ") | fields group_value strongest_evidence | eval top_pipe=1 ] | eventstats values(strongest_evidence) as strongest_evidence by group_value | where isnull(top_pipe) | eval fw_item=if(governance_mapped=1,dm_frameworks,"__unmapped__") | mvexpand fw_item | eval fw_item=if(fw_item="__unmapped__",null(),fw_item) | stats first(matched_dm_fields) as matched_dm_fields dc(datamodel) as matched_datamodel_count values(fw_item) as mapped_frameworks dc(eval(if(is_primary_dm=1,datamodel,null()))) as high_relevance_dm_count dc(eval(if(governance_mapped=1 AND is_primary_dm=0,datamodel,null()))) as supporting_dm_count dc(eval(if(governance_mapped=0,datamodel,null()))) as unmapped_dm_count values(strongest_evidence) as strongest_evidence max(governance_mapped) as governance_mapped by group_value | eval high_relevance_dm_count=coalesce(high_relevance_dm_count,0) | eval supporting_dm_count=coalesce(supporting_dm_count,0) | eval unmapped_dm_count=coalesce(unmapped_dm_count,0) | eval strongest_evidence=if(isnull(strongest_evidence) OR strongest_evidence="", "-", strongest_evidence) | eval mapped_frameworks=if(isnull(mapped_frameworks),"None",mvjoin(mvsort(mapped_frameworks),"; ")) | eval datamodel_footprint=high_relevance_dm_count . " primary, " . supporting_dm_count . " supporting, " . unmapped_dm_count . " unmapped" | rename group_value as Source strongest_evidence as "Strongest primary evidence" datamodel_footprint as "Observed datamodel footprint" matched_dm_fields as "Matched CIM fields" mapped_frameworks as "Mapped frameworks" | table Source "Strongest primary evidence" "Observed datamodel footprint" "Matched CIM fields" "Mapped frameworks" | sort - "Matched CIM fields" Source

div.p: What this shows: Which governance frameworks are represented by the selected telemetry based on configured datamodel mappings.
Why it matters: Shows which frameworks this Data Source population touches most broadly, beside the recommended-field completeness charts above.
Read it as: Higher bars mean more distinct sources overlap that framework’s mappings. Mapping evidence only, not a compliance assertion.

div.p: What this shows: Detailed framework-to-capability-to-datamodel mapping evidence behind the executive coverage and source-level governance indicators.
Why it matters: This panel exposes the rationale, confidence and field evidence used to support governance coverage calculations.
Read it as: Each row is supporting evidence for review and validation. It should be used to understand how DIG reached a result, not as a standalone compliance conclusion.

div.p: What this shows: The calculation model used to connect governance frameworks, control areas, DIG capabilities, Splunk datamodels and observed telemetry evidence.
Why it matters: Each control uses one High-relevance primary datamodel for completeness scoring. Additional mapped models stay Medium-High or lower as supporting evidence.
Read it as: Completeness bands are Good / Partial / Low / No Coverage on recommended CIM fields. This supports governance conversations but does not replace formal compliance assessment.
